title: Incident comms briefing cookbook (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, copy-paste friendly templates and a compact war-room checklist for incident communications. This is a working cookbook — lightweight, pragmatic, and intentionally informal so on-call engineers can iterate fast.

Audience assumptions:
- Internal war-room (sre-oncall@redwood, infra-eng slack)
- Product & CS leads (PM, CS-Support)
- External: customers via status page + per-customer comms when impacted SLAs exist

Severity shorthand (for use in templates):
- Sev1: Major outage impacting >50% of customers or blocking core product flows (inference API down).
- Sev2: Significant degradation for a subset of customers or elevated error rates/latency.
- Sev3: Minor degradation, feature-level issues, or single-customer impact with workaround.

Quick rules of thumb for comms:
- First internal signal: 5–10 minute initial slack + war-room invite + create incident ticket (Jira RNW-xxxx).
- First external (status page): within 15 minutes of confirmed user-impact for Sev1/Sev2, within 60 minutes for Sev3 if customers affected.
- Always include three lines: TL;DR, Impact, Next update ETA.
- Avoid speculative causes. Use "investigating" until verified.

Status page update templates (copy/paste)
1) Initial (immediate) 
Title: Degraded inference API / Investigating
Body: TL;DR: We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts for Redwood hosted inference endpoints.
Impact: Some requests to the /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints are returning 5xx or timing out. Estimated affected traffic: unknown / likely subset.
What we know: Error rates increased at ~{{HH:MM UTC}}; error codes: 502/504 and client timeouts.
What we're doing: Team is triaging, collecting traces, and isolating impacted fleet.
Next update: {{+15m}} or earlier if new info.

2) Follow-up (confirmed degradation, actionable)
Title: Partial service degradation affecting inference latency and errors
Body: TL;DR: Partial degradation affecting requests routed to region-east (GPUs X/Y).
Impact: ~30% of inference requests may see latency >2s or 5xx errors. Customers with dedicated capacity unaffected unless specified.
What we know: Root cause candidate: degraded kernel on instance pool gpu-east-3; CPU/mem normal; retry rates rising.
What we're doing: Draining gpu-east-3, failing over to gpu-east-4, and increasing autoscale threshold. Engineers running circuit-breaker patch.
ETA: mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes.

3) Resolution
Title: Service restored — incident resolved
Body: TL;DR: The issue affecting inference endpoints is resolved.
Impact: Latency and error rates returned to baseline. No customer data exposure detected.
What we did: Drained and reprovisioned affected instances; deployed a transient fix to kernel selection; rolling validation across regions.
Post-incident: Full postmortem planned; ETA for postmortem: {{date}}.

Customer-facing email template (for dedicated/enterprise customers)
Subject: Incident update — Partial degradation impacting inference ({{date}})
Hi {{CustomerName}},
We wanted to let you know about an incident that affected inference performance for a subset of traffic starting at {{HH:MM UTC}}. Our team identified elevated error rates and latency for requests routed to a GPU pool in us-east and performed a controlled failover.
What this meant for you: If you saw increased latency or errors, retries should have recovered requests; dedicated customers on reserved pools were not impacted unless specifically indicated.
What we did: Drained affected hosts, reprovisioned, and applied a temporary kernel fallback.
Next steps: We will share a detailed post-incident report within 72 hours. If you need immediate support or a customer-level RCA, reply to this email or open a ticket referencing RNW-1587.
Regards,
Aisha Patel
Redwood Inference — SRE

Internal Slack/War-room snippets (short messages)
- CHANNEL: #sre-oncall (pinned)
Initial: [INCIDENT RNW-1587] Investigating increased 5xx/timeouts for /v1/generate. War-room: https://meet.link/warroom-1587. Please join if you are on-call.
Status (30m): [RNW-1587] Partial degradation confirmed. Draining node pool gpu-east-3 -> failing over. Running health-checks on gpu-east-4.
Customer comms (to PM/CS): Draft sent to customers impacted by dedicated pools. ETA for next external update: 30m.
Post-resolution: [RNW-1587] Resolved. Logging for RCA. Please do not send external comms until postmortem draft approved by comms/legal.

War-room checklist (quick actionable list)
1) Create incident ticket + severity and link it to runbook. (owner: oncall)
2) Start war-room (record link) and invite: oncall, infra-shift, product-ops, CS-lead, engineering manager. (owner: oncall)
3) Baseline metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by code, request volume, autoscale events, GPU health summaries. (owner: telemetry)
4) Identify blast radius: list affected clusters/pools/accounts (owner: infra)
5) Mitigation options: failover, scale-out, throttling, circuit-breaker, rollback. Attempt safe mitigations first. (owner: eng)
6) Customer segmentation: which customers/tenant IDs hit the bad pools? Trigger direct emails for enterprise customers. (owner: cs)
7) Legal/comms check: if PII or SLA breach suspected, notify legal immediately. (owner: oncall)
8) Prepare status page initial update and assigned writer. (owner: comms)
9) Update cadence: internal every 15 min (Sev1) or 30 min (Sev2). External per status page cadence. (owner: comms)
10) After mitigation: collect logs, snapshots, traces; freeze related deploys until postmortem. (owner: eng)

Roles & responsibilities (short)
- On-call SRE: overall incident lead, author initial status updates, coordinate mitigation.
- Infra engineer: node pool & hardware ops, failover/drain actions.
- Telemetry owner: graphs, real-time dashboards, validate metrics.
- Product/PM: customer escalation decisions, messaging alignment.
- CS/Support lead: customer notifications and one-off support.
- Legal/Trust: advise on data exposure and regulatory steps.

Decision log template (inline)
[Time UTC] [Decision maker] — [Decision] — [Rationale] — [Rollback trigger]
Example: 2024-11-02 18:12 UTC — On-call (Aisha) — Drained gpu-east-3 and shifted traffic to gpu-east-4 — Rationale: avoid further 5xx; Rollback if p95 latency on gpu-east-4 > 2s for 10m.

Handoff to PM/CS checklist (post-mitigation)
- Confirm customer-impact list (tenant IDs) and severity per customer.
- Draft customer email (template above) and share with PM/CS for approval.
- Schedule customer-level RCAs for affected enterprise accounts if requested.
- Note any credits/SLAs triggers.

Post-incident communications timeline (recommended)
0-1h: internal war-room + status page initial note.
1-6h: follow-up status page updates as we make progress; customer-level emails where applicable.
24-72h: postmortem draft (internal) for review.
72-120h: public postmortem (sanitized) and direct customer RCA if needed.

Phrases to avoid (comms hygiene)
- Avoid: "root cause was..." until validated. Avoid technical speculation.
- Prefer: "preliminary root cause indicates" or "investigations show signals consistent with".

Metrics to include in updates (minimum)
- Error rate baseline vs current (5xx, 4xx), total request volume, p95 latency, % of traffic affected, number of customers impacted (est).

Approval gating (when to involve legal/comms/customer success)
- Legal: suspected data exposure, PII, regulatory scope.
- Comms: incidents that will be public-facing beyond status page (press/customer briefings).
- CS: enterprise contract holders affected or SLA miss.

Examples of short TL;DR lines (pick one)
- "Investigating elevated errors for inference endpoints, mitigation in progress."
- "Partial degradation in us-east GPU pool; failover underway."
- "Service restored; validating metrics and preparing postmortem."

Open questions / TODOs (draft hygiene)
- Should we automate the status page push from incident ticket metadata? (tech debt)
- Can we add per-customer impacted list export to telemetry to speed targeted emails?
- Add checklists for on-prem/private customers where network isolation changes the failover semantics.

Notes from last usage (brief)
- During RNW-1473 we under-communicated the blast radius. Action: require explicit customer-impact list in first 30m.
- Keep status updates machine-readable header for automation: [INCIDENT:RNW-####] [SEV:1] [ETA:+15m]

Appendix: sample automation-friendly status header (copy/paste)
[INCIDENT:RNW-1587] [SEV:2] [ETA:+30m] TL;DR: Partial degradation — failing over node pool gpu-east-3.

End of draft. Please comment inline or ping me on #sre-runbooks for quick edits.
